abstract: We characterize, in the worst case over kernels, the sharp minimax width of online confidence intervals for elements of a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS). This resolves the open problem posed by Vakili et al. (2021) in its original discrete-time form. A learner observes $y_i=f(x_i)+ε_i$ at adaptively chosen points, with $\|f\|_{\mathcal H_k}\le B$ and i.i.d. $R$-sub-Gaussian noise, and reports the interval $|f(x)-μ_n(x)|\leρ_n(δ)σ_n(x)$, where $μ_n$ and $σ_n$ are the posterior mean and standard deviation of a surrogate Gaussian process model with regularization parameter $λ$. Writing $ρ_n^*(δ)$ for the minimax confidence width for a fixed kernel, we show that, for the sum of a linear kernel and a periodic Sobolev kernel, all sufficiently large $n$, and all $δ\in(0,1/4]$, $ρ_n^*(δ)\asymp B+(R/λ)\sqrt{γ_n+\log(1/δ)}$, where $γ_n$ is the maximal information gain and grows polynomially in $n$. Building on Lattimore (2023), we construct an adaptive design on a fixed two-dimensional domain for which, under Gaussian noise, the normalized error at a prespecified point is $Ω(B+(R/λ)\sqrt{γ_n})$ with constant probability. This rules out the conjectured polylogarithmic width in the worst case over kernels and online designs.

title: Tight Sequential Confidence Intervals for Online Kernel Regression
